Two types of samples were selected: those in the as-fabricated (AF) condition.

Structure_Text.original: The IPF maps indicated a nearly random distribution of grain orientations... fine equiaxed grains and coarse columnar grains. Statistical results revealed that the average sizes of fine equiaxed grains were measured to be 1.49 μm for the AF sample... while the average sizes of coarse columnar grains were found to be 1.84 μm for the AF sample... EDS map obtained from the equiaxed grain area of the AF sample revealed the stacking of Cu-rich and Sc-rich precipitates along the equiaxed grain boundaries. Structure_Text.simplified: AF sample: nearly random grain orientation (max texture intensity 2.79). Fine equiaxed grains avg 1.49 μm, coarse columnar grains avg 1.84 μm. Grain boundaries decorated with Al₂Cu and AlCuSc precipitates (avg 116±42 nm at GB in equiaxed area, 117±32 nm at GB in columnar area). Intra-granular precipitates within columnar grains avg 42±13 nm. Al₃(Sc,Zr) nucleant particles too small for TEM-EDS distinction. Zr supersaturated in Al matrix in columnar grain areas.

The HT samples underwent gradual heating at a rate of 10 °C/min from room temperature to reach 300 °C inside a KSL-1400X muffle furnace. Subsequently, they were held at 300 °C for 1 h before cooled to ambient temperature in air.

Process_Text.original: A gas-atomized alloy powder, comprising Al-3.89Cu-1.22Li-0.98Sc-0.43Zr (wt%), was employed as the feedstock for the LPBF process using a LiM-X260A LPBF machine. Samples with a relative density exceeding 99.9% were fabricated under laser power of 300 W, scanning velocity of 1200 mm/s, hatch spacing of 0.1 mm, and layer thickness of 40 μm. The HT samples underwent gradual heating at a rate of 10 °C/min from room temperature to reach 300 °C inside a KSL-1400X muffle furnace. Subsequently, they were held at 300 °C for 1 h before cooled to ambient temperature in air.
Process_Text.simplified: Gas-atomized Al-Cu-Li-Sc-Zr powder processed by LPBF (LiM-X260A) at 300 W, 1200 mm/s, 0.1 mm hatch, 40 μm layer. Heat treatment: heated at 10 °C/min from RT to 300 °C, held 1 h, air cooled.

Structure_Text.original: The IPF maps indicated a nearly random distribution of grain orientations in both samples. Statistical results revealed that the average sizes of fine equiaxed grains were measured to be 1.53 μm for the HT sample, while the average sizes of coarse columnar grains were found to be 1.76 μm for the HT sample. The comparative grain sizes implied no significant grain coarsening after heat treatment. For the HT sample, an increased number of precipitates can be observed in both equiaxed grain area and columnar grain area. The fine precipitates within the columnar grains tended to coalesce and grow, resulting in a size increase to 72 ± 21 nm. The precipitation particles were nearly continuously stacked along the grain boundaries in the HT sample. These precipitates located at the grain boundaries exhibited sizes of 125 ± 39 nm for equiaxed grains and 123 ± 37 nm for coarse grains, which were respectively larger by approximately 8% and 5% compared to those presented in the AF sample.
Structure_Text.simplified: HT sample: nearly random grain orientation (max texture intensity 1.83). Fine equiaxed grains avg 1.53 μm, coarse columnar grains avg 1.76 μm. No significant grain coarsening after heat treatment. Increased number of Al₂Cu and AlCuSc precipitates. Intra-columnar-grain precipitates avg 72±21 nm (71% growth vs AF). GB precipitates: 125±39 nm (equiaxed), 123±37 nm (columnar). Nearly continuous stacking along GBs vs intermittent in AF.
